rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act – unconscionable rent increase limit
rules.requirement: A rent increase must not be unconscionable (so unreasonable as to shock the conscience of a fair and honest person) and must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases. Before evicting for nonpayment of an increased rent, the owner must first serve a valid notice to quit and notice of rent increase.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants facing a rent increase in New Jersey; the State has no laws that establish, govern or control rents, but municipalities may pass rent control or rent leveling ordinances.
rules.penalty: If an increase is unconscionable or proper notice was not given, the tenant may file a complaint with a municipal rent control board where one exists; where there is none, a judge decides in an eviction action for nonpayment whether the increase is unconscionable.
rules.quoted_span: The increase in rent must not be unconscionable; it must not be so unreasonable as to shock the conscience of a fair and honest person and must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases.
rules.interaction_text: must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases

rules.title: Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Law – exemption from local rent control
rules.requirement: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from any local rent control ordinances for 30 years following completion of construction of the building.
rules.quoted_span: Under the Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Law ( N.J.S.A. 2A:42 -84.5), newly constructed multiple dwellings shall be exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period of 30 years following completion of construction of the building.
rules.interaction_text: newly constructed multiple dwellings shall be exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period of 30 years following completion of construction of the building

rules.title: No rent increases to cover condominium/cooperative conversion costs
rules.requirement: When a building is converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership of units, rents may not be increased to cover costs resulting solely from the conversion; increases to cover new services or amenities are not barred.
rules.coverage_text: All tenants in a building converted to a condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership of units, regardless of whether they are eligible for protected tenancy as senior citizens or disabled persons.
rules.exemptions: Rents may still be increased to cover the cost of new services or amenities.
rules.quoted_span: If a building is converted to a condominium or cooperative form of ownership, or to fee simple ownership of units, rents may not be increased to cover cos ts resulting solely from the conversion (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.31).

rules.title: NJHMFA-controlled rents exempt from municipal rent control
rules.requirement: Rents fixed and controlled by the New Jersey Housing and Mortgage Finance Agency in projects it finances are not subject to municipal rent control ordinances.
rules.coverage_text: Projects financed by the New Jersey Housing and Mortgage Finance Agency whose rents it fixes and controls.
rules.citation: New Jersey Housing and Mortgage Finance Agency (NJHMFA)
rules.quoted_span: Likewise, rents fixed and controlled by the New Jersey Housing and Mortgage Finance Agency (NJHMFA) in projects it finances are not subject to municipal rent control ordinances.
rules.interaction_text: are not subject to municipal rent control ordinances
